order_tables.title: Approved Truing Up of account for the year 2019-20
headers: As per Truing Up Petition (Rs. lakh)

power_purchase.kserc_reasoning: In view of the approval of actual distribution loss of 1.41% as mentioned in Para 17 of this order, the Commission hereby approves the purchase of 565.80 lakh units from KSEB Ltd at a cost of Rs.3582.29 lakh for the year 2019-20.
key_observations: Licensee paid excess demand charges of Rs.16.05 lakh to KSEB Ltd.
New PPA with 13000 kVA contract demand effective from 23-03-2020, no excess demand charge thereafter.
power_purchase.methodology_applied: Approved as claimed, considering actual distribution loss and allowing excess demand charges due to no fault of licensee.

employee_cost.kserc_reasoning: Since the actual employee cost is within the norms fixed, the Commission hereby approves the actual employee expenses of Rs.138.96 lakh for the year 2019-20. The O&M expenses, which includes Employee costs (Rs.138.96 lakh), R&M expenses (Rs.5.20 lakh), and A&G expenses (Rs.29.73 lakh) totalling to Rs.173.89 lakh is the actuals for the year 2019-20. However, this amount is lower than the O&M expenses of Rs.201.49 lakh approved as per the Regulations. Hence there is a gain of Rs.27.60 lakh (Rs.201.49 lakh – Rs.173.89 lakh). The Commission had allowed to retain the benefit of efficiency gain to the licensee in the year 2018-19. Similarly, in the year 2019-20 also the petitioner has incurred O&M expenses lesser than the norms fixed and accordingly eligible for the benefit as per Regulation 14 of Tariff Regulations 2018. Hence, the Commission hereby approves Rs.192.29 lakh as the Operation and Maintenance expenses for the year 2019-20.
key_observations: Actual employee cost is lower than norms approved by the Commission.
Overall O&M expenses resulted in an efficiency gain of Rs.27.60 lakh.
2/3rd of efficiency gain (Rs.18.40 lakh) is retained by the licensee as per Regulation 14 of Tariff Regulations 2018.
employee_cost.methodology_applied: Approved actual employee expenses as claimed, then applied efficiency gain sharing as per Regulation 14 to total O&M, which was reflected in the employee cost line item in the final summary.

repair_maintenance.kserc_reasoning: The Commission has duly considered the licensee's submission. Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves the actual amount of Rs.5.20 lakh as R&M for the year 2019-20.
key_observations: Actual claim is lower than the norms in Tariff Regulations, 2018.
Decrease of Rs.7.04 lakhs in R&M expense compared to previous year.

admin_general.kserc_reasoning: Considering the details furnished by the licensee, the Commission hereby approves the actual amount of Rs.29.73 lakh as the Administrative and General expenses for the year 2019-20.
key_observations: Claimed amount is Rs.1.74 lakhs higher than the level specified in the Regulation.
Increase in insurance cost due to higher premium for Fire Policy and Machinery breakdown premium.
Increase in charges for monitoring and managing prepaid metering system.
admin_general.methodology_applied: Approved actual amount as claimed. Directed licensee to take steps to bring prepaid metering system expense to acceptable levels by tendering.

depreciation.kserc_reasoning: The licensee has claimed depreciation for the entire assets, though the licensee is not eligible for depreciation on the assets created out of the accumulated surplus. The Commission while Truing Up of Accounts for 2018-19 had approved an amount of Rs.33.85 lakh as depreciation after duly considering the assets added till 2015-16. On this basis, the depreciation approved for the purpose of Truing Up of Accounts for the year 2019-20 after deducting the depreciation on assets created out of accumulated regulatory surplus as shown below: Accordingly, against a claim of Rs.76.93 lakh in the Truing Up of account petition, the Commission hereby approves the depreciation of Rs.36.65 lakh for the year 2019-20.
key_observations: Depreciation is not allowable on assets created out of accumulated surplus (Rs.606.67 lakh).
depreciation.methodology_applied: Deducted depreciation applicable to assets created from accumulated surplus from the total claimed depreciation.

interest_long_term.kserc_reasoning: The licensee has not claimed any interest and finance charges for 2019-20.
interest_long_term.methodology_applied: Not applicable as no claim was made.

interest_consumer_deposits.kserc_reasoning: Since the licensee is following the pre-payment metering system, interest on working capital is also not allowable.
interest_consumer_deposits.methodology_applied: Not allowable due to pre-payment metering system.

return_on_nfa.kserc_reasoning: While Truing Up the accounts for the year 2018-19, the Commission had approved an amount of Rs.17.84 lakh as against Rs.37.79 lakh claimed by the licensee. The licensee has created assets from 2016-17 using their accumulated surplus. Since the same has no cost of funds, the return on NFA is not allowable for the said assets. Accordingly, the NFA eligible for return is as shown below. As shown above, after deducting the assets created out of accumulated surplus, the RoNFA eligible for the year 2019-20 is Rs. 16.82 lakh. Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves the amount of Rs.16.82 lakh (3% of Rs.560.82 lakh) as return on net fixed assets for the year 2019-20.
key_observations: Assets created from accumulated surplus have no cost of funds.
Return on NFA is not allowable for assets created from accumulated surplus.
return_on_nfa.methodology_applied: Calculated 3% RoNFA on Net Fixed Assets after deducting assets created out of accumulated surplus.

other_debits.kserc_reasoning: The Commission therefore directs the licensee to submit the complete details of all deposits held in the distribution business along with details of interest received within 3 months of the date of this order. Hence, the Commission provisionally approves the non tariff income of Rs.124.36 lakh as claimed by the licensee for Truing Up of Accounts of 2019-20.
key_observations: Licensee yet to provide details of deposits/sources for differential income of Rs.51.04 lakh.
Reduction in interest on security deposit due to lower bank rate.
other_debits.methodology_applied: Provisionally approved as claimed, pending submission of further details.

energy_decision.kserc_reasoning: As shown above, the Commission hereby approves the distribution loss at 1.41%. Since this excess distribution loss is meagre, no adjustment in power purchase cost is made.
energy_decision.excess_demand_action: Under such circumstances, and taking due cognizance of the fact that excess demand charges had to be paid by the licensee for no fault of theirs, the Commission has decided to follow the same position taken in the previous Truing Up Order (dated 18-12-2020) and the Commission hereby allows the Excess Demand Charges of Rs.16.05 lakh.

capital_structure_verified.kserc_reasoning: The Commission after considering the items of capital expenditure of Rs.3.76 lakh and the submissions by the petitioner to justify this expenditure, approves Rs. 3.76 lakh for inclusion in the asset base, subject to the condition that the licensee is not eligible for depreciation and other financing costs on the said items. The Commission has decided to retain the approved cost for the solar PV plant as per Order dated 02-12-2019, i.e., Rs.405.45 lakh. The Commission notes that the funds utilised were from the accumulated regulatory surplus and no additional funding was received during the year. The licensee did not furnish any documents indicating that the funds are fresh infusion of capital into the distribution business. Hence, the funds utilised are nothing but the accumulated surplus. The accumulated regulatory surplus is over and above the regulated return and reasonable expenses including efficiency gains allowed by the Commission to the licensee. Hence, the said surplus belongs to the consumers and is meant to be adjusted against the consumer tariffs in future. Since such frequent tariff adjustment process is not undertaken due to uniform retail tariff, such surplus is allowed to be retained by the licensee as a source of investment funds for future. Hence, if any financing cost such as depreciation or interest charges are allowed for such surplus funds, it would result in double payment by the consumers. Hence, the licensee is not eligible for any financing costs such as interest charges or depreciation on the utilisation of such surplus for creation of assets.
